links.targetTitle: Genesis Primitives seal themselves after a single Invocation

title: Genesis Primitives are single-use by construction, so no further Instances can ever be Invoked
content:
Across A.6.1.1.7.2.1, three Genesis Primitives — Agent Creation (A.6.1.1.7.2.1.1), Prime Transformation (A.6.1.1.7.2.1.2), Executor Transformation (A.6.1.1.7.2.1.3) and Agent Token (A.6.1.1.7.2.1.4) — all carry the same closing statement in both their Hub and Instance trees: the Primitive "is deployed solely for the one-time creation of the Agent" (or transformation, or "one-time deployment of the Agent's token"), and therefore "no further Instances of the Primitive can be Invoked."

The same reasoning is used to empty the Operational Process Definition: "no further operational process is needed post-deployment."

The pattern separates two classes of Primitive with different lifetimes. Genesis Primitives are constitutive — they bring the Agent, its type, and its token into existence, and once that has happened re-running them is not merely unnecessary but structurally forbidden. Operational Primitives, by contrast, are re-invocable machinery the Agent uses continuously.

What makes this load-bearing rather than bookkeeping is that the prohibition is written into the Artifact, not left implicit. A future proposal to re-invoke Agent Creation or re-run Prime Transformation would have to edit the Artifact text that says it cannot be done, making identity changes visible as Artifact edits rather than as ordinary operations.
description: Agent Creation, Prime Transformation and Agent Token Primitives each run exactly once; the Atlas closes their In-Progress Invocation directories and drops post-deployment process entirely.
